ev.q: Experience of one to two ACEs was associated with poorer mental health and increased suicidal behaviors
Nearly three quarters (73.1%) of high school students aged <18 years reported at least one ACE during the COVID-19 pandemic
Compared with adolescents without ACEs, adolescents who reported one to two ACEs during the pandemic had higher prevalences
After adjusting for all other assessed ACEs and demographic characteristics, emotional abuse was most strongly associated
First, the cross-sectional nature of the data does not permit causal inferences in associations

methods_quotes.q: Adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and 95% CIs were calculated using Poisson regression with robust SEs
aPRs were adjusted for sex, grade in school, race and ethnicity, sexual identity, and method of school instruction at recruitment into ABES
Weighted pairwise prevalence estimates and 95% CIs for reported ACE exposure by poor mental health or suicidal behaviors were calculated.
95% CIs that excluded 1.0 were considered statistically significant.
Analyses were conducted using SAS statistical software (version 9.4, SAS Institute), accounting for complex survey design.
